subject: Consumption velocity & latency impact summary
messages:
From: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@starline.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Trevor Simmons <trevor.simmons@starline.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Q1 telemetry & sudden token velocity increase

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the call last week. Attaching our Q1 telemetry export so the team can see the raw usage patterns. Two quick highlights from our side: 1) token velocity for our conversation API jumped ~2.3x starting Apr 2 (see "avg_tokens_per_min" column), and 2) 95th percentile latency increased from 180ms to ~420ms on peak windows.

We suspect a combination of a feature experiment (wider context windows) and a recent customer batch that increased parallel inference. We're approaching the committed capacity cushion and want to understand options — brief term extension? burst credits? or moving to a larger Dedicated pool?

Attached: starline_q1-telemetry.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)

Can your team run a quick ROI/lifecycle readout and recommend a short runway we can present to the execs? We're targeting a renewal conversation the week of May 3.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Gupta
Head of Platform
Starline AI

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya Gupta <maya.gupta@starline.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q1 telemetry & sudden token velocity increase

Hi Maya — thanks for sending the telemetry. I pulled the CSV and did a surface pass with Ben and Laura. Short answer: we're seeing a predictable tradeoff between token velocity and per-token unit economics, and the latency bump looks like queuing at tail windows rather than model degradation.

Next steps I propose so we can get you a succinct recommendation for the execs:
- Ben will run a short cost uplift model comparing (A) short term burst credits + modest extension vs (B) rightsize to a larger Dedicated tranche and quantized model profile. Expect rough delta to committed monthly spend.
- Laura will validate latency traces and correlate with peak concurrency windows; if queuing, we can propose an autoscale/burst-flow that buys headroom without a full tranche commitment.
- I will draft a 1-page ROI readout showing monthly spend delta, expected latency improvements, and recommended rollout plan (canary + fallback).

Proposed timeline: deliverables by Fri Apr 23 EOD PT and then a 30-min sync (May 4 or May 5) to present recommendations. Is May 4 at 10am PT okay for you?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Principal, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Q1 telemetry & sudden token velocity increase — initial analysis

Hannah / Laura / Maya — attaching a quick draft proposal (proposal_draft_v2.pdf) and a terse set of calculations. Topline findings from a 90-minute analysis:

1) Token mix shift: ~45% of the additional tokens are coming from larger context windows in a small (12%) set of heavy sessions. If Starline can apply a context-length tier for those sessions, projected token spend reduces by ~18% without changing model configs.

2) Cost delta: if you take the short runway option (2 months burst credits + 1-month top-up), estimated incremental spend = +$28k/month on average, with minimal SLA change. If you upgrade to a dedicated NPU pool + quantized model variant, estimated incremental spend = +$50k/month but reduces p95 latency to ~210ms and improves token unit cost by ~22%.

3) Operational suggestion: a hybrid approach — immediate burst credits to avoid throttles, concurrent rollout of quantized variant in canary to validate QA. If canary passes, schedule dedicated tranche start aligned with next billing cycle.

I've left margin assumptions in the PDF. If Hannah wants, I can convert the PDF into a one-pager for execs tomorrow.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
